decision: One BFF per client type (consumer GraphQL with persisted queries, store GraphQL with offline sync, ops REST with RBAC, partner REST with webhooks)
why: Each client has different shapes, auth and failure modes; a single API would serve none of them well and couple every release.
alternative: One general-purpose API gateway with shared endpoints.
value: Teams change their client's API without coordinating with the other three.

decision: Every service owns its database, chosen for its access pattern (ledger-grade RDBMS for orders and credit, MongoDB + Redis for stock, Postgres for commission, Redis streams for notifications)
why: Shared databases turn every schema change into a cross-team negotiation and every slow query into everyone's outage.
value: Catalog reads 3–5× faster and independent deploys (2 → 8–12 per week in the real system).

decision: Services publish through an outbox table read by a CDC relay into Kafka, keyed by business id
why: Writing to the database and the broker separately loses events on partial failure; the outbox makes both one commit.
alternative: Publish from application code after commit.
value: No lost or phantom events, and every event can be replayed.

decision: Packets are real world events following their real route, and hover shows each hop's golden signals
why: A static box diagram says what exists; moving traffic shows how it flows and where it hurts.
value: Reviewers see the system behave, not just its boxes.

decision: Each replay narrates the incident step by step, then can run it live across every zone and deep-links to the screens that react
why: An incident is a story across systems; running it live proves Counter, Pay, Mesh and Tidewatch agree.
value: Architecture and product are shown as one system.

decision: Open-source technology keeps its name; commercial vendors are shown as roles (enterprise RDBMS, work queues, fan-out topics, CDN + WAF)
why: The portfolio names only fictitious companies; roles also keep the design portable across clouds.
value: Honest about the architecture without endorsing or impersonating vendors.
